title: World Portal
status: Merged, published, served-byte verified, public portal/AR gameplay accepted and downloaded release restored. Physical-device and player-quality approval remain open.

changes.portal: Replaces the finite six-plane world crop with a per-eye fragment ray/box aperture. The existing 3D expedition remains visible beyond side and rear faces, up to the normal camera far plane, while fragments outside the projected box or before its entrance are rejected. This is continuous rendering of the existing world, not a new asset-streaming system, flat render texture or second simulation.
changes.centering: The courier remains exactly at the focus mapped to the room-fixed box anchor. The world moves around the courier. Behind-character presentation follows deliberate pad/desktop look; tracked pointing is separated from table orbit and head motion never steers the courier.
changes.box: Existing physical dimensions, scale and height preferences, recenter placement and three legal top/front openings remain. Default footprint is 1.80 by 1.44 meters. Near-facing shell panels are transparent per eye; other shell faces use a faint non-occluding tint rather than terminating the world.
changes.maskCoverage: Stock meshes, instancing, skinned humans, custom shaders, sprites, lines, particles and asynchronously loaded materials use the same aperture. Each draw uses the full inverse camera/projection and actual viewport, including the scaled XR rig. Tracked device and UI subtrees are excluded from world masking even when desktop preview precedes XR.
changes.ui: Diorama status is docked below the box. The explicit spatial menu anchors when opened and does not follow head roll or lean. No persistent full menu plane covers ordinary diorama gameplay.
changes.goal: The map draws a larger goal marker last, plus NEXT, distance and elevation. Its dashed line is explicitly a bearing, not a guaranteed walkable route. A depth-tested world beacon and spatial status use the existing tracked-objective resolver without changing progress.
changes.firstPersonAR: New explicit First-person AR / life-size passthrough option requests immersive-ar. Life-size gameplay retains collision and controls while opaque sky, background and fog are removed for alpha composition. Exit restores ordinary rendering. No physical-room, furniture or obstacle sensing is provided.
changes.entry: Open XR / diorama views from the start screen, pause menu or Settings. Choose Third-person diorama AR / passthrough, Third-person diorama VR, First-person AR / life-size passthrough, or the retained First-person VR before entering XR. Exit XR before changing session type. Desktop diorama preview remains available without a headset.
changes.siblingReference: Adapted the same-repository Dino Atlas ray/box portal principle to Aether's scaled camera and material lifecycle. No sibling runtime was changed.

sourceFindings: Two existing UI planes were parented to the camera.
The previous clipping pass excluded custom shader materials.
corrections: Move diorama HUD and explicit menus out of head-following placement.
Apply a depth-preserving aperture to custom and billboard shaders as well as standard materials.
Use actual per-draw eye matrices and viewports and keep tracked devices outside the mask.
rectangleDiagnosis.evidence: GPU coverage tests and actual-application synthetic head lean, yaw and roll checks pass. Downward, rolled and lateral stereo captures were reviewed.
rectangleDiagnosis.limit: The source causes are corrected, but no physical Quest was available to conclusively attribute the user's observed rectangles to only one cause or certify their absence on that device.

preserved.handTracking: Both tracked hands operate spatial UI. Hand-only combat and locomotion remain unsupported.
preserved.concurrency: Normal expected-head merge retained the separate archive-workflow update. Final comparison through master 1e416ee0872b4f0268eab1ebb90a1ad019e41cf9 found only unrelated theology additions after the game merge, with no intervening Aether or root chooser changes.
preserved.scope: No user browser storage was cleared and no world area, mission, enemy, collectible or reward was added by this presentation release.

native.additionalPortalChecks: Seven GPU cases and 23 application checks also passed in the dedicated exact-head workflow; not added again to the main total.
native.prRegressions: All 11 Aether PR regression workflows on the accepted head completed successfully, including supplemental grounded run35277953030. Their duplicate checks are not added to the main total.
native.gpuResults: Seven isolated framebuffer fixtures cover front/side full depth, roll, scaled stereo viewports, custom shader and billboard coverage. No pre-entry geometry survives. At most one sampled boundary pixel differs from CPU interval expectations, within the declared eight-sample tolerance. No shader errors.
native.scope: Native HTTP software WebGL with ordinary DOM or synthetic Gamepad/XR inputs. The GPU fixture is a rendering fixture, not a gameplay playthrough. Game journeys do not assign actor position, health, inventory, missions or rewards to manufacture acceptance. No physical hardware or human-quality approval.

additionalViewReview.scope: Actual application with synthetic downward/rolled/lateral headset poses and reviewed stereo captures. This audit source differs only in the later application-test exit helper, not runtime bytes. Not physical Quest certification.

publicGameplay.scope: Separate actual public HTTPS application. Includes map, centered movement, deliberate camera follow, save preservation, explicit portal AR, head isolation, box-fixed status, anchored menu, both hands, pinch interaction, life-size AR, Xbox movement, hidden-session pause and spatial Exit. Supported Light graphics selected through Settings at full 960x640 pixel density. Synthetic devices, not physical-device certification.

backup.scope: Public game snapshot and evidence, not player browser saves, private story, full Git mirror or independent off-site backup.

retainedFailures: Strict source-transfer validation rejected one duplicated character before promotion. The original payload hash remained mandatory; no transfer scaffolding remains in the release tree.

First application attempt passed21 checks then tried a desktop Exit button blocked by the legitimate pause modal. Failed artifact10520428668 is retained with SHA-256 2a7b6ebcb09ba113064aa4ddf8e91d74970f2771bf814be50ba7f50acd804815. The corrected fixture uses genuine spatial Exit and opens pause explicitly after hand Resume, without forced clicks or state assignment.
Source review found desktop preview could accidentally register XR-device materials before first immersion. Explicit subtree exclusion and a regression test fix this ownership boundary.
Local HTTP Chromium was administratively blocked and is not counted as browser success. Native and public browser evidence came from GitHub runners.

A local publication-archive inspector initially assumed flat members; the known nested manifest was explicitly allowed and fully reconciled. A local repeat-test launcher also hit log-directory ownership after restore; unchanged tests were then run successfully through the container. Neither audit correction changed game or CI acceptance rules.

Superseded incomplete runs remain distinct from the accepted exact-head run. A narrowly scoped obsolete-run audit found no active eligible runs and cancelled nothing. No completed evidence or sibling job was deleted.
unverified: Headset comfort, readability and sustained performance
